:::{#def-precision-matrix}

#### Precision of a random vector (precision matrix)

The **precision matrix** of a $p \times 1$ [random](random-variables.qmd#def-random-variable) vector $\vX$
extends the [precision](#def-precision) of a [random variable](random-variables.qmd#def-random-variable)
to a vector:
it is the [matrix inverse](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/linear-algebra-special-matrices.html#def-matrix-inverse)
of the [variance matrix](#def-cov-vec-x) of $\vX$,
just as the precision of a random variable is the reciprocal of its [variance](#def-variance).
It is defined when $\Varf{\vX}$ is
[positive definite](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/linear-algebra-special-matrices.html#def-positive-definite):

$$\precision(\vX) \eqdef \inv{\Varf{\vX}}.$$

For $p = 1$, $\precision(\vX)$ is the precision $\inv{\Var{X}}$ of the single variable $X$.

:::
